{{Short description|Mexican astronomer}}
{{Use dmy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=December 2022}}
{{Use list-defined references|date=December 2022}}
{{Family name hatnote|Allen|Armiño|lang=Spanish}}
'''Christine Patricia Allen Armiño''' is a Mexican astronomer whose research has included [[runaway stars]] including the [[Becklin–Neugebauer Object]],{{ran|A}}{{ran|D}} the overall distribution of mass in the [[Milky Way]] and its effects on stellar orbits,{{ran|B}} [[star system|binary and multiple star systems]],{{ran|C}} and the applications of [[binary star]] observations in testing physical theories.{{ran|E}} She is a senior researcher at the Institute of Astronomy of the [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]], and the editor of the ''Mexican Magazine of Astronomy and Astrophysics''.{{r|unam}}

The galactic mass distribution model she developed with Alfredo Santillán{{ran|B}} has been called the Allen–Santillán model.{{r|bb16}}

==Recognition==
Allen is a member of the [[Mexican Academy of Sciences]].{{r|amc}} UNAM gave her their Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz prize in 2008.{{r|awards}}
